pr.title: Prototype Touch ID from a detached process for session unlock
pr.head: c0ec100ed177de647198c9813977be3c184f559d

summary: The session-unlock plan designs a background agent: after you type the passphrase once, a process started by the multipass command holds the store's vault key in memory, and every later read or change asks for a Touch ID touch instead of the passphrase. The agent calls setsid, so it leads a session of its own with no controlling terminal and keeps running after the command and its terminal exit.

The plan could not be marked ready until one question in its § 6.5 was answered: does macOS's LocalAuthentication framework show its Touch ID sheet for such a detached process? If it did not, the agent would have had to stay in the terminal's session, and the plan would have changed.

This pull request answers it with a prototype. probe.rs is one Rust file, built with rustc outside the crate, that calls LocalAuthentication the way the future src/touch_id.rs will. run.sh builds it and asks for three touches: one from the terminal, one from a child that called setsid, and one from a child with only its own process group. The owner ran it on Apple silicon with macOS 27.0.1, and the sheet appeared and was approved all three times. So the plan keeps setsid, records the results in § 6.5, and moves from draft to ready.
Nothing here changes multipass itself: Cargo finds no target under docs/, cargo tree still lists only multipass, and no CI job runs the script.

cards.title: Terms on this page
cards.html:
• LocalAuthentication: Apple's framework that shows the Touch ID sheet and reports whether a person approved it.
  • LAContext: the framework's object for one authentication; canEvaluatePolicy asks whether approval is possible, and evaluatePolicy shows the sheet.
  • Policy 4: LAPolicyDeviceOwnerAuthenticationWithBiometricsOrWatch, a finger or a paired Apple Watch, with no fallback to the login password.
  • setsid: the system call that puts a process in a new session with no controlling terminal.
  • Global block: an Objective-C block (a closure) that captures nothing and lives forever, so the runtime never copies or frees it.

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html:
• One open finding: run.sh close, the test the implementation must run by hand for a request after the terminal closes, starts its child with spawn group rather than setsid, so it tests the fallback the plan dropped.
  • Two wording suggestions on § 6.5's SSH and Apple Watch cases.
  • The probe was built with rustc -D warnings but not run, because it shows a real Touch ID sheet. CI passed.

groups.title: The Touch ID probe
groups.kicker: A one-file Rust program that calls LocalAuthentication as the agent will
intro: The probe is the shape src/touch_id.rs will take. It loads LocalAuthentication with dlopen, as src/clipboard.rs loads AppKit, so the framework is in the process only when needed. It calls LAContext through objc_msgSend cast to each method's exact type, because on Apple silicon a variadic call passes arguments in the wrong registers.

evaluatePolicy answers through an Objective-C block on a queue the framework owns. The probe builds that block by hand from the block ABI's layout, as a global block that captures nothing, and the block sends the result to the waiting thread through a channel kept in a static.

Its modes are can (ask whether each policy can be evaluated), evaluate (show the sheet), noui (evaluate with interaction not allowed, which fails at once with no sheet and so tests the block safely), and spawn setsid|group, which starts a detached copy of itself running one of those modes, writes the result to a file, and exits, as the CLI will.

files.note: The whole prototype: framework loading, typed message sends, the hand-built reply block, and the detached spawn.

checks.text: Built cleanly with rustc --edition 2024 -O -D warnings into a temporary directory, and rustfmt --check passes. It was not run, because it shows a real Touch ID sheet.
The policy values 1 to 4 match Apple's LAPolicy declarations, and policy 4 never falls back to the login password, as plan § 2.8 requires.
The block literal's fields (isa, flags, reserved, invoke, descriptor) follow the block ABI's order, and BLOCK_IS_GLOBAL is 1 << 28.
On timeout the probe calls invalidate, which makes the framework deliver the pending reply with LAErrorAppCancel; the probe waits five more seconds for it.
spawn setsid runs setsid between fork and exec. The real agent calls it itself after it starts, which has the same effect because a forked child is never a group leader.

groups.title: The sheet test script
groups.kicker: Builds the probe and asks for three touches, attached and detached
intro: run.sh builds the probe into target/touch-id-prototype/, which Git ignores, and runs three requests: one attached to the terminal, one from a setsid child, and one from a child with only its own process group. For each detached child it waits up to 75 seconds for the result file to end with done. A person must be at the Mac to touch the sensor, so nothing runs it automatically.
run.sh close is a separate test for a request that arrives after you close the terminal window: it starts a child that waits 15 seconds before asking, so you can close the window first.

files.note: The hand-run sheet test, and the closed-terminal test the implementation must still run.

checks.text: bash -n and sh -n pass, the script sets set -euo pipefail, and every path is quoted. shellcheck was not available.

Open finding: run.sh close starts its child with spawn group, which keeps the terminal as its controlling terminal. § 6.5 says the agent keeps setsid and that this test checks the closed-terminal case, so it should spawn with setsid.

groups.title: The plan's decision
groups.kicker: § 6.5 records the results, keeps setsid, and the plan goes ready
intro: The plan's status moves from draft to ready, which claims the plan can be built as written. With § 6.5 decided, questions 6.1 to 6.5 all are.

§ 6.5 now holds a table of what the prototype showed, and three cases it did not test: a request after the terminal window closes, canEvaluatePolicy over SSH, and an Apple Watch approval. Each fails toward a denied request or a passphrase prompt, never toward exposing the store, so the implementation checks the first two by hand instead of the plan waiting on them.
§ 2.11's row for src/touch_id.rs now says it loads the framework with dlopen rather than linking it, matching the clipboard module.

files.note: Status to ready, § 6.5's results and remaining cases, and the § 2.11 row for src/touch_id.rs.

checks.text: The readiness flip owns every question open at the flip. All of § 6 is decided, and § 6.5's three untested cases each name their fail-safe outcome, so none blocks readiness.
§ 6.5, the SSH case: § 2.1 step 3 already starts no agent when SSH_CONNECTION is set, so this hand check matters only for a login without it. A review suggestion asks the text to say so.
§ 6.5, the Apple Watch case: § 2.8 treats 60 seconds with no answer as denied and only no watch in reach as unavailable. A review suggestion asks this line to say "out of reach".
